The most common win left on "EMERALD MINE 9X" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and eight of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The numbers for "EMERALD MINE 9X" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
5055.headline: Prize table details

5057.body:
"EASY MONEY" has 415,091 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with two left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If "EASY MONEY" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
5057.headline: The prize table, line by line

5059.body:
"THE CASH WHEEL" has had no $1 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "THE CASH WHEEL" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
5059.headline: No new top prize claims

5060.body:
"FIND THE 7S" paid out its last $50,000 prize six months ago. The ticket still advertises it because printed tickets never change. Prize tables do change, and the biggest prize listed today is $10,000.

Everything above about "FIND THE 7S" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
5060.headline: Big prize shown, none left

5063.body:
One of CA$H IN HAND's top prizes was claimed two days ago. A player in Florida won $2 million. The game started with four top prizes and now has two top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

If "CA$H IN HAND" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
5063.headline: Fewer $2 million prizes left
